The reported results support readiness under the Phase 1 clear-air criterion, not unrestricted readiness. Omitting the marine-layer results would materially overstate demonstrated performance.

**Executive Readiness Summary**

The system met the Phase 1 clear-air detection criterion, detecting methane plumes in 40 of 40 trials at 500 meters. According to Dr. Sterling’s interpretation, the Phase 1 protocol defines readiness using clear-air performance; confirmation of that interpretation requires reference to the controlling protocol and applicable agreement.

In separate marine-layer testing above 75% relative humidity, the system detected 8 of 14 plumes and missed 6. These results do not alter the reported clear-air Phase 1 result, but they limit the evidence for operation under high-humidity marine-layer conditions.

**Conclusion:** The system has demonstrated Phase 1 readiness for the tested clear-air conditions at 500 meters. Readiness for marine-layer conditions above 75% relative humidity has not been demonstrated.

Before release, verify the criterion and any legal characterization against the signed Phase 1 protocol rather than relying solely on an oral interpretation.
